text: After this you can compare an energy project with both a discounted result and a realistic range of outcomes.

Use a cash-flow timeline when yearly costs, replacement spending, and savings vary. Choose a study period and a discount rate that match the decision. Net present value adds discounted future net benefits and subtracts the initial cost. A positive result is not a guarantee because input values remain estimates. Compare alternatives on a compatible service basis and study period. Test low, central, and high savings cases before a recommendation.

items: Inferred: Illustrative calculation: A project costs $1,200 and saves $500 at each of three year-ends. At 10% per year, NPV is -1200 + 500/1.1 + 500/1.1² + 500/1.1³, about $43.43.
